newsitem.title: USA: White House aide hails Mexico as top drug fighter.
newsitem.headline: White House aide hails Mexico as top drug fighter.

text.p: Mexico has launched what may be the world's most aggressive drive to wipe out opium poppies and marijuana, the White House national drug control chief said on Wednesday.

"They have become essentially the leading nation of the world on the eradication of illegal drugs," the official, retired Army General Barry McCaffrey, said at a joint news conference with Mexico's new attorney general, Jorge Madrazo Cuellar.

Citing U.S. figures, McCaffrey credited Mexico with having wiped out roughly 8,500 hectares (21,000 acres) of opium and about 12,000 hectares (30,000 acres) of marijuana in 1995. Eradication last year had continued at a "comparable rate," he said.

McCaffrey, who praised Madrazo as a "noted legal scholar, a human-rights activist and a man of absolute integrity," has tended to use lavish praise to oil the gears of U.S.-Mexican cooperation on drug matters.

At the news conference, he said Madrazo's new anti-drug coordinator, retired Lt. General Jose Gutierrez Rebollo, had a reputation similar to Madrazo's, calling him an "honest man and no-nonsense" former army field commander.
"Let me tell you, up front, we are proud of our association with these two public servants," McCaffrey said.

He said Mexican seizures of cocaine, heroin and marijuana had soared in the last 10 months, with heroin captures up 78 percent from the year before. He also praised recent arrests of suspected drug lords and closer law enforcment cooperation with the United States.

Madrazo, Mexico's seventh attorney general in eight years, was named to the job in December. He replaced Antonio Lozano Gracia, dismissed by President Ernesto Zedillo for incompetence along with many of the antidrug officials with whom McCaffrey had been working. McCaffrey had been lavish in his praise of the old team as well.
